title: Ramified strict reduction tensor balancing with its universal counit
statement: Use finite integral coefficients, constant tower tensor $T$ [def-pur-constant-scalar-tower-mates], and the native reduction restricted to constants $D_E,D_F$ and its ordinary/derived whole-system counits [def-pur-native-constant-support-model]. Let $E\subset F$, choose $e\ge1$ with $\varpi_E\mathcal O_F=\varpi_F^e\mathcal O_F$, and use the actual completed inclusion $C=-\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_E}\widehat{\mathcal O}_F$ and its ramified quotient maps [def-pur-finite-compact-support-scalar-data]. Positive tower index $n$ is encoded by $n+1$; let $s_e$ retain index $e(n+1)$ with composite transitions. Define the ordinary natural isomorphism between tensor by $B$ of the ordinary $E$ reduction and $s_e$ of the ordinary $F$ reduction of ordinary completed scalar extension by the local formula $b\otimes(1\otimes x)\mapsto1\otimes(b\otimes x)$, with the constant section $b$ mapped into completed coefficients. Define $\kappa:D_ET\cong CD_Fs_e$ as the unique natural isomorphism such that, on every completed-module cochain complex $P$, $\kappa_{Q(P)}$ followed by the target whole-system counit equals the source whole-system counit followed by localization of that specified ordinary balancing. This normalization is imposed before finite evaluation, rather than selecting maps in independently derived fiber categories.

proof.text: At each module and quotient index use the single-level pure-tensor normalized isomorphism. These local witnesses are used inside the theorem proof only, never to define public data from mere existence.

Prove unit naturality from adjunction-unit naturality and limMap_π, and prove its horizontal compatibility from limit.w. The normalized scalar adjunction and tensor scalar multiplication imply naturality of pure tensors. The source generator criterion proves horizontal commutativity of the chosen level maps and then their naturality in M. Assemble first with NatIso.ofComponents in the tower index, then in M. The same generator criterion proves uniqueness of the resulting natural isomorphism.

Apply the independent source and target counit universal properties to obtain the two natural cochain counits with their exact displayed components. No arbitrary witness defines data: these local witnesses are used only in a theorem proof.

Apply the ordinary balancing isomorphism degreewise and then Q to identify the two ordinary composite functors. Mathlib rightKanExtensionUniqueOfIso constructs the derived isomorphism. Its lift factorization gives the counit equation on every complex. For uniqueness apply Iso.ext and hom_ext_of_isRightKanExtension to the target counit, reducing to the prescribed equations on every complex.
